title: Simple interrupted sutures
references: Standard surgical skills teaching on simple interrupted skin sutures: entering at a right angle to the skin, following the needle's curve, equal bites either side of the wound, even spacing
todo: Confirm the target bite distance, depth and spacing for a pad of these layer thicknesses and this needle size.
Confirm the number of throws in the knot for the suture material the pad represents.

feedback.outside_wound: That bite was not beside the wound. Place each suture along the cut.
feedback.missed_far_side: The needle came back up inside the wound, so it never caught the far edge. Enter further from the edge, or more upright.
feedback.too_shallow: The bite stayed in the skin. Take the needle down into the fat beneath, or the edges can gap.
feedback.too_deep: The needle went down into the fascia. A skin bite should stay above it.
feedback.angle_toward: The needle leaned toward the wound as it went in. Enter at a right angle to the skin.
feedback.angle_away: The needle leaned away from the wound as it went in. Enter at a right angle to the skin.
feedback.bite_narrow: The needle went in close to the edge, where the stitch can tear through.
feedback.bite_wide: The needle went in far from the edge, which bunches the tissue.
feedback.asymmetric: The needle came out a different distance from the edge than it went in, so the two edges will sit at different heights.
feedback.off_curve: The needle was pushed off its curve instead of turned along it.
feedback.knot_loose: A throw slipped, so the knot may not hold.
feedback.spacing_wide: Two sutures are far apart, leaving a gap between them.
feedback.spacing_uneven: The gaps between the sutures vary a lot.
feedback.depth_uneven: The bites went to different depths.
